title: Monthly Principal Labour Force Statistics, Seasonally Adjusted
description: Seasonally adjusted monthly principal labour force statistics, including unemployment and participation rates.

fields.name: date
fields.title: Date
fields.description: [Date] The date in YYYY-MM-DD format, with DD set to 01 since the data is at monthly frequency

fields.name: lf
fields.title: Labour Force Size
fields.description: [Float] Seasonally adjusted number (in thousands) of employed and unemployed individuals. This figure also represents the number of people participating in the labour force.

fields.name: lf_employed
fields.title: Employed Persons
fields.description: [Float] Seasonally adjusted number (in thousands) of people who worked at least one hour for pay, profit or family gain, in thousands of people

fields.name: lf_unemployed
fields.title: Unemployed Persons
fields.description: [Float] Seasonally adjusted number (in thousands) of people who did not work but were looking for work or available to work

fields.name: u_rate
fields.title: Unemployment Rate
fields.description: [Float] Seasonally adjusted ratio of unemployed to labour force size

fields.name: p_rate
fields.title: Participation Rate
fields.description: [Float] Seasonally adjusted ratio of the labour force size to the working-age (15-64) population

methodology: This data is produced based on the Labour Force Survey (LFS), which is designed to collect representative data on the labour force at national and state level. Consistency in methodology has been maintained to ensure that the data is comparable over time. Survey findings are a monthly, quarterly and annual basis. For a full description of the methodology, in particular the seasonal adjustment methodology, please refer to the [Technical Notes](https://open.dosm.gov.my/publications/technical-notes/lfs-technotes).
caveat: Data prior to 2025 is compiled in concordance with population data from the 2010 Census. Data from 2025 onwards is compiled in concordance with population data from the 2020 Census. As such, you may observe a trend break in the series due to the different references used. Furthermore, sums of each category may not always equal to the totals shown in related tables because of independent rounding to one decimal place. However, the differences are not obvious.
publication: The [Labour Force Report, Jun 2026](https://open.dosm.gov.my/publications/labour_month_2026-06), the latest edition of the monthly labour force statistics published by DOSM. OpenDOSM also features a [dashboard on the labour force](https://open.dosm.gov.my/dashboard/labour-market).
